pull_request.title: prove: ktest in rcu
pull_request.body:
The rest ktest code in sync module cannot be proved.

This PR 
- Completes the reference–permission and alignment specifications in sync::rcu::non_null.
- Adds new third party spec for `<NonNull<T> as core::cmp::PartialEq>::eq`
~~Separates linear Arc ownership permissions from borrowed read permissions, preventing duplicate ownership recovery and borrowed-to-owned permission escalation.~~
~~Preserves Arc allocation identity across raw-pointer conversions. Borrowed handles use ManuallyDrop to avoid incorrectly decrementing the reference count.~~
- Keeps Arc ownership permissions private and linear, preventing duplicate ownership recovery through the modeled owning conversion API.
- Documents the unresolved Arc allocation-identity and borrowed-conversion verification limitations.
pull_request.bodyHTML:
The rest ktest code in sync module cannot be proved.

This PR

  • Completes the reference–permission and alignment specifications in sync::rcu::non_null.
  • Adds new third party spec for <NonNull<T> as core::cmp::PartialEq>::eq
    Separates linear Arc ownership permissions from borrowed read permissions, preventing duplicate ownership recovery and borrowed-to-owned permission escalation.
    Preserves Arc allocation identity across raw-pointer conversions. Borrowed handles use ManuallyDrop to avoid incorrectly decrementing the reference count.
  • Keeps Arc ownership permissions private and linear, preventing duplicate ownership recovery through the modeled owning conversion API.
  • Documents the unresolved Arc allocation-identity and borrowed-conversion verification limitations.

review_comments.body:
This carries ownership permissions across `Arc` raw-pointer conversions. `'a` bounds a borrowed permission, while `T` remains `'static`.

`None` represents a freshly wrapped owner; `Some` contains either an owned permission or its borrow. The permission also preserves allocation identity.

`ManuallyDrop` prevents borrowed handles from decrementing the strong count, and `into_arc` requires ownership. Owning handles must be consumed explicitly; otherwise they leak. I've clarified this in the documentation.

And `arc_from_raw` and `arc_into_raw` will just consume this token.

review_comments.body:
`Exclusive` would enforce linear ownership, but the current private-field `tracked` token already provides that.

The remaining issue is allocation identity: after `arc_from_raw` consumes the token and returns a plain `Arc<T>`, its original pointer is no longer represented in the model. A later `arc_into_raw` cannot establish pointer equality, since Verus models `Arc<T>` by its pointee value.

So GPT doesn't think changing the token alone is sufficient to remove `ArcWithPtr`.

review_comments.body:
I tried this approach: removed `ArcWithPtr`, added an uninterpreted `ptr()` method for `Arc<T>`, and connected it to the raw-pointer conversion specs. Full verification passed.

However, GPT also found a counterexample: Verus proves that the pointers returned from two independent `Arc::new(42u32)` allocations are equal, while executing the same function returns `false`.

GPT tested this implementation, but found that the current Arc model equates Arcs with equal pointee values, which also forces their uninterpreted `ptr()` results to be equal. How should allocation identity be modeled to avoid this issue?

review_comments.body: So what is blocking the verification?
review_comments.body_html: So what is blocking the verification?
review_comments.body_text: So what is blocking the verification?

review_comments.body:
The blocker is allocation identity. The current Verus model can equate two `Arc<T>` values with equal pointee values, even when they belong to different allocations. After restoring a plain Arc from a raw pointer, the specs preserve its value but cannot establish that converting it back returns the original pointer. This blocks the pointer-equality assertion in `Either::left_pointer`.

`ArcWithPtr` carries that identity as ghost state, together with the raw-pointer permission. It also distinguishes owned permissions from borrowed ones: only an owning handle can become an ordinary, independently droppable Arc. Borrowed handles use `ManuallyDrop` to avoid decrementing the strong count.

Without the wrapper, borrowed construction is another blocker: `raw_as_ref` has a borrowed permission, while the existing `arc_from_raw` contract requires consuming an owning permission.

Adding an uninterpreted `ptr()` to plain Arc does not resolve this: equal Arc values would necessarily have equal `ptr()` results, incorrectly identifying distinct allocations.

Here uses `#[verus_spec]` outside a `verus!` block, so this expression needs the macro's rewriting.
